questions.explanation: Glucose has six carbon atoms and an aldehyde group (-CHO) in the open chain form, so it is an aldohexose. Fructose, which has a ketone group at C-2, is the ketohexose, and ribose is an aldopentose.

optionRationale.1: A ketohexose has a ketone group; this describes fructose, not glucose.
optionRationale.3: Glucose has six carbons, not five.
optionRationale.4: Glucose has six carbons and an aldehyde group, not five carbons and a ketone group.

questions.objective: Classify monosaccharides by carbonyl group and chain length

questions.stem: Which of the following vitamins is soluble in water?
questions.explanation: Vitamin C and the B-group vitamins are water soluble, so they are excreted in urine and must be supplied regularly in the diet. Vitamins A, D, E and K are fat soluble and are stored in the liver and adipose tissue.

optionRationale.1: Vitamin A is fat soluble and is stored in the liver.
optionRationale.2: Vitamin D is fat soluble and is stored in the body.

questions.stem: How many chiral carbon atoms are present in the open-chain structure of D-fructose?
questions.explanation: Open-chain fructose is HOCH$_2$-CO-CHOH-CHOH-CHOH-CH$_2$OH. The carbons C-1 and C-6 are CH$_2$OH groups and C-2 is the carbonyl carbon, none of which is chiral. Only C-3, C-4 and C-5 carry four different groups, so there are 3 chiral centres.

optionRationale.1: Four chiral centres are present in glucose, which has an aldehyde carbon at C-1 and so has C-2 to C-5 chiral.
optionRationale.2: Three secondary alcohol carbons are chiral; two is an undercount.
optionRationale.3: Five would include the carbonyl carbon and one CH$_2$OH carbon, which are not chiral.

questions.stem: Glucose is oxidised with bromine water. The main organic product is
questions.explanation: Bromine water is a mild oxidising agent and oxidises only the aldehyde group of glucose to a carboxylic acid, giving gluconic acid. This also shows that the carbonyl group of glucose is an aldehyde. Stronger nitric acid oxidises both ends to give saccharic acid.

optionRationale.2: Saccharic acid needs the stronger oxidant, concentrated nitric acid, which oxidises both -CHO and the terminal -CH$_2$OH.
optionRationale.3: Sorbitol is formed by reduction of glucose, not oxidation.
optionRationale.4: n-Hexane is formed by prolonged heating of glucose with HI, which is a reduction.

questions.objective: Know the product of mild oxidation of glucose

questions.stem: Which of the following amino acids is optically inactive?
questions.explanation: Glycine, NH$_2$CH$_2$COOH, has two hydrogen atoms on its alpha carbon, so that carbon is not attached to four different groups. It has no chiral centre and is optically inactive. Alanine, valine and serine have a chiral alpha carbon.

optionRationale.1: Alanine has CH$_3$ on the alpha carbon, which makes it chiral.
optionRationale.3: Valine has an isopropyl group on the alpha carbon, which makes it chiral.
optionRationale.4: Serine has a CH$_2$OH group on the alpha carbon, which makes it chiral.

questions.objective: Identify the only achiral standard amino acid

questions.stem: Glycine is dissolved in a solution whose pH is much lower than its isoelectric point, and an electric field is applied. In what form does glycine mainly exist and in which direction does it migrate?
options: As a zwitterion, with no net migration
As an anion, towards the anode
As a cation, towards the cathode
As a cation, towards the anode
questions.explanation: At pH below the isoelectric point the carboxylate group of the zwitterion is protonated, giving $^+$NH$_3$CH$_2$COOH. This species carries a net positive charge, so it moves towards the negatively charged cathode in an electric field.

optionRationale.1: The zwitterion dominates only near the isoelectric point, not in strongly acidic solution.
optionRationale.2: The anion exists in solutions of pH above the isoelectric point.
optionRationale.4: A cation is attracted to the cathode, not the anode.

questions.objective: Relate pH and isoelectric point to the charge on an amino acid

questions.stem: How many different tripeptides can be formed from three different amino acids if each amino acid is used exactly once in each tripeptide?
questions.explanation: A tripeptide has an N-terminal and a C-terminal end, so the sequence matters. Three different amino acids can be arranged in 3! = 6 ways, for example Gly-Ala-Val and Val-Ala-Gly are different tripeptides.

optionRationale.1: Three counts only the choice of the first residue and ignores the order of the other two.
optionRationale.2: Nine is 3 x 3 and does not come from arranging three distinct units.
optionRationale.3: Twenty-seven (3$^3$) would be correct only if each amino acid could be repeated.

questions.objective: Count peptide sequences from distinct amino acids

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Vitamin C can be stored in the human body for a long period.
Reason (R): Vitamin C is a water-soluble vitamin.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Vitamin C is water soluble, so the reason is true. Water-soluble vitamins are readily excreted in urine and are not stored, so they must be supplied regularly in the diet. The assertion is therefore false. Fat-soluble vitamins such as A and D are the ones stored in the body.

optionRationale.1: The assertion is false, so (R) cannot explain it.
optionRationale.2: The assertion is false, so this option is wrong.
optionRationale.3: The reason is true: vitamin C is water soluble.

questions.objective: Link solubility of vitamins with storage in the body

questions.stem: Match the amino acid in List-I with its feature in List-II.
questions.explanation: Aspartic acid has two carboxyl groups and one amino group, so it is acidic (A-III). Lysine has two amino groups and one carboxyl group, so it is basic (B-IV). Glycine has hydrogen as its side chain (C-I). Cysteine contains a sulphur thiol group (D-II).

optionRationale.2: This code interchanges the matches of A and B; the correct pairs are A-III and B-IV.
optionRationale.3: This code interchanges the matches of C and D; the correct pairs are C-I and D-II.
optionRationale.4: This code interchanges the matches of A and C; the correct pairs are A-III and C-I.

questions.objective: Match amino acids with the features of their side chains

right: I. Side chain is a single hydrogen atom
II. Side chain contains a thiol (-SH) group
III. Acidic amino acid with an extra -COOH group
IV. Basic amino acid with an extra -NH$_2$ group

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about enzymes.
A. Enzymes are biological catalysts, and most of them are globular proteins.
B. An enzyme lowers the activation energy of the reaction it catalyses.
C. Most enzymes lose their activity when heated to a high temperature.
D. The activity of an enzyme is independent of the pH of the medium.
Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Enzymes are protein catalysts that provide a lower-energy path, and they are denatured by heat. Each enzyme works best at an optimum pH and temperature, so statement D, which says that activity is independent of pH, is wrong.

optionRationale.1: Statement D is wrong, and C is also correct, so this selection is wrong.
optionRationale.3: Statement D is wrong and statement A is correct, so this selection is wrong.
optionRationale.4: It includes the wrong statement D and omits the correct statements B and C.

questions.objective: Recall the general properties of enzymes
